result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick a small set, explain the seasonal comparison and cover the layout well. B is ahead on the money question: it adds cost per visit on a rolling 12 months and adjusts the budget plan for bills that arrive in lumps. It also defines active cardholders precisely, while A's 'percent of town' still seems to count inactive cards. A gives slightly stronger reasons for what it leaves off and a richer layout, but those don't outweigh B's better caveats on misleading measures and its fuller treatment of finances. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers pick a short list, give each measure a sensible yardstick and explain why same-period-last-year comparisons handle seasonality. A covers the money question better: it adds a rolling 12-month cost per visit alongside budget vs plan, and it fixes the inactive-cardholder problem by counting only cards used in the last 12 to 24 months. B points out the inactive-card flaw but then uses a percentage of the town that still includes inactive cards, and it has only one finance measure, though its layout advice is very practical.
